# gba-emu: rules for every agent

Read PLAN.md before starting. It defines the phases, the shared contracts and who owns which file.
The benchmark lives at `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.
Use that absolute path; relative paths break inside worktrees.

## Originality (hard rule)
- Write all code yourself. Do not read, copy, or paraphrase any existing emulator:
  `$GBA_EVAL/candidates/` (gba-core), `$GBA_EVAL/third_party/` (Mesen2),
  `$GBA_EVAL/reference/mesen_step.cpp`, or mGBA/NanoBoyAdvance/VBA/etc. from memory or the web.
- Allowed sources: `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gbatek.htm` (GBA, ARM and THUMB chapters only), `$GBA_EVAL/spec/ABI.md`,
  `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gba_bios_stub.h`, the grader's outputs (scores, `.ref.png` vs `.cand.png`),
  and running ROMs from `$GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms/`.
- No per-ROM hacks: never branch on a ROM's hash, title, or game code. Fix the hardware behavior.

## Code readability
- Use clear, descriptive names for functions, variables and types: `destination_register`, `shift_amount`,
  `fn execute_data_processing`. Never cryptic ones like `x`, `t`, `rd2` or `tmp`. Loop indices
  (`i`, `line`) are fine when the meaning is obvious.
- Official gbatek register and field names are allowed (`DISPCNT`, `BG0CNT`, `IE`, `IF`, `CPSR`, `Rd`, `Rn`),
  each with a short plain-English comment where it is defined, e.g. `const DISPCNT: u32 = 0x000; // display control`.
- Every non-obvious function gets a one-line doc comment naming the gbatek section it implements, e.g.
  `/// Barrel shifter for data-processing operand 2 (gbatek: ARM Opcodes: Data Processing (ALU)).`
- Prefer small readable functions over clever one-liners. Split a long `match` arm or a dense bit-twiddling
  expression into a named helper.

## Ownership
- Only edit the files your task owns (see the ownership tables in PLAN.md).
- Shared files (`src/lib.rs`, `src/gba.rs`, `src/bus.rs`, `src/io.rs`, `src/irq.rs`, `src/scheduler.rs`,
  `Cargo.toml`) are changed only by the integrator (the executor session). If you need a contract
  change, say so in your report instead of making it.

## Git
- Remote: https://github.com/Rohan-Jalil/gba-eval-trial-rohan. Never push; the human pushes.
- Author and committer: Rohan Jalil <[REDACTED:email]>. This is set in this repo's git config;
  do not override it.
- Use Conventional Commits: `type(scope): summary`, for example `feat(cpu): add ARM data-processing ops`,
  `fix(ppu): wrap affine BG coordinates`, `test(timer): cascade overflow`, `docs(notes): phase 1 decisions`,
  `chore(results): phase 1 milestone`. Scopes: cpu, arm, thumb, bus, io, irq, ppu, apu, dma, timer,
  keypad, cart, abi, scripts, plan, notes, results.
- Commit after every meaningful step (a working instruction group, a passing test, a merged branch),
  not one large commit per phase.
- Worker agents commit on their own branch. Only the integrator merges into `main` (`git merge --no-ff`).

## Logging
- `NOTES.md`: add an entry for every decision or change of approach (date, what, why), and for every
  phase record which agents ran and on which model. The integrator writes the agent/model rows.
- `TIMELOG.md` belongs to the human. Agents never edit it.
- Milestones: `scripts/grade-full.sh <phase> "<note>"` saves `results/milestones/<phase>/`. Commit that
  folder and `scores.tsv`. All other `results/` output stays ignored.

## Before you report done
1. `cargo test` passes.
2. `cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` succeeds.
3. `scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm <name> <your tests> <smoke set>`.
   Report the per-test scores, and never lower a smoke-set score without saying so.
4. Your work is committed on your branch, and your report lists the commits.

# gba-emu build plan

Goal: an original Game Boy Advance emulator in Rust, built as `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, exporting the 10
functions in `gba-eval/spec/ABI.md`, that scores above the 0.534 baseline on the gba-eval grader. The
grader's highest reachable score is 0.96, because the `comprehensive` subsystem carries weight but has no tests.

Paths in this document are relative to this repo (`gba-trial/gba-emu`). The benchmark repo is
`/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.

## Scope: must-have vs stretch

| Phases | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | **Must-have** | Skeleton, CPU, interrupts/timers/DMA, full graphics. Each one finished, gated and verified with a milestone grade before the next starts. |
| 4-6 | **Stretch** | Sound, game compatibility/timing, performance. Started only once Phase 3 is verified, and dropped if time runs out. |

A solid, verified 0-3 is worth more than a broken 0-6. Never start a stretch phase while a
must-have gate is failing, and never leave `main` in a state that does not build or that scores lower
than the last milestone.

---

## 1. How the score is made (what to optimise)

| Section | Weight | Tests | Scoring |
|---|---|---|---|
| Replay | 60% | 11 homebrew games with recorded input | Mean per-frame SSIM vs Mesen2 over thousands of frames. Drifting out of sync ruins every later frame. |
| Procedural | 20% | 16 test ROMs | Only the final frame counts, and it must be almost pixel-exact (pass/fail). |
| Audio | 20% | 9 of the replays | Per-frame log-mel spectrum vs Mesen2. Silence scores 0. |

Procedural subsystem weights: cpu 0.35, comprehensive 0.20 (no tests, always 0), memory 0.15,
timer 0.12, halt_irq 0.10, dma 0.08. Audio: psg 0.5, game_audio 0.5.

Consequences:
- **CPU correctness comes first.** Every other test depends on it.
- **The PPU (graphics) carries the most weight**, because all 11 replays are graphics comparisons.
- **Timing accuracy matters a lot**, because replay inputs land on fixed frame numbers. If the game boots
  a few frames later than in Mesen2, every button press lands at the wrong moment.
- **Colour precision is forgiving.** The grader quantises to 5 bits per channel, so any sensible
  5-to-8-bit colour expansion is fine.

---

## 2. Architecture and shared contracts (Phase 0, one agent, before any parallel work)

Everything that more than one agent touches is defined here first. Parallel agents then work only inside
their own files, which is what keeps merges conflict-free.

One crate, `gba_emu`, with `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]`. The `rlib` lets `cargo test` and a native
debug binary run on the host without wasm.

  lib.rs          ABI exports only (the 10 functions), thin wrappers over a single global Gba
  gba.rs          Gba struct: owns every component, run_frame() main loop
  bus.rs          memory map: read8/16/32, write8/16/32, region dispatch, returns access cycles
  io.rs           IO register dispatch table: address range -> owning component
  irq.rs          IE / IF / IME, request(IrqSource), pending() -> bool
  scheduler.rs    cycle counter; components are stepped by "cycles elapsed"
  cpu/mod.rs      Cpu struct, register file, modes, banking, CPSR/SPSR, exceptions, step()
  cpu/alu.rs      barrel shifter, add/sub with flags, condition evaluation
  cpu/arm.rs      ARM (32-bit) decode + execute
  cpu/thumb.rs    THUMB (16-bit) decode + execute
  ppu/mod.rs      line timing, DISPCNT/DISPSTAT/VCOUNT, line compositor, framebuffer
  ppu/bg_text.rs  tiled backgrounds (modes 0-2)
  ppu/bg_affine.rs rotation/scaling backgrounds
  ppu/bitmap.rs   modes 3/4/5
  ppu/obj.rs      sprites (normal + affine)
  ppu/effects.rs  windows, blending, mosaic
  timer.rs        4 timers, prescaler, cascade, overflow IRQ, FIFO tick

GBA Sound Channel 1 - Tone & Sweep
4000060h - SOUND1CNT_L (NR10) - Channel 1 Sweep register (R/W)
  Bit        Expl.
  0-2   R/W  Number of sweep shift      (n=0-7)
  3     R/W  Sweep Frequency Direction  (0=Increase, 1=Decrease)
  4-6   R/W  Sweep Time; units of 7.8ms (0-7, min=7.8ms, max=54.7ms)
  7-15  -    Not used
Sweep is disabled by setting Sweep Time to zero, if so, the direction bit
should be set.
The change of frequency (NR13,NR14) at each shift is calculated by the
following formula where X(0) is initial freq & X(t-1) is last freq:
  X(t) = X(t-1) +/- X(t-1)/2^n
4000062h - SOUND1CNT_H (NR11, NR12) - Channel 1 Duty/Len/Envelope (R/W)
  Bit        Expl.
  0-5   W    Sound length; units of (64-n)/256s  (0-63)
  6-7   R/W  Wave Pattern Duty                   (0-3, see below)
  8-10  R/W  Envelope Step-Time; units of n/64s  (1-7, 0=No Envelope)
  11    R/W  Envelope Direction                  (0=Decrease, 1=Increase)
  12-15 R/W  Initial Volume of envelope          (1-15, 0=No Sound)
Wave Duty:
  0: 12.5% ( -_______-_______-_______ )
  1: 25%   ( --______--______--______ )
  2: 50%   ( ----____----____----____ ) (normal)
  3: 75%   ( ------__------__------__ )
The Length value is used only if Bit 6 in NR14 is set.
4000064h - SOUND1CNT_X (NR13, NR14) - Channel 1 Frequency/Control (R/W)
  Bit        Expl.
  0-10  W    Frequency; 131072/(2048-n)Hz  (0-2047)
  11-13 -    Not used
  14    R/W  Length Flag  (1=Stop output when length in NR11 expires)
  15    W    Initial      (1=Restart Sound)
  16-31 -    Not used
  GBA Sound Channel 2 - Tone
This sound channel works exactly as channel 1, except that it doesn't have a
Tone Envelope/Sweep Register.
4000068h - SOUND2CNT_L (NR21, NR22) - Channel 2 Duty/Length/Envelope (R/W)
400006Ah - Not used
400006Ch - SOUND2CNT_H (NR23, NR24) - Channel 2 Frequency/Control (R/W)
For details, refer to channel 1 description.
  GBA Sound Channel 3 - Wave Output
This channel can be used to output digital sound, the length of the sample
buffer (Wave RAM) can be either 32 or 64 digits (4bit samples). This sound
channel can be also used to output normal tones when initializing the Wave RAM
by a square wave. This channel doesn't have a volume envelope register.
4000070h - SOUND3CNT_L (NR30) - Channel 3 Stop/Wave RAM select (R/W)
  Bit        Expl.
  0-4   -    Not used
  5     R/W  Wave RAM Dimension   (0=One bank/32 digits, 1=Two banks/64 digits)
  6     R/W  Wave RAM Bank Number (0-1, see below)
  7     R/W  Sound Channel 3 Off  (0=Stop, 1=Playback)
  8-15  -    Not used
The currently selected Bank Number (Bit 6) will be played back, while
reading/writing to/from wave RAM will address the other (not selected) bank.
When dimension is set to two banks, output will start by replaying the
currently selected bank.
4000072h - SOUND3CNT_H (NR31, NR32) - Channel 3 Length/Volume (R/W)
  Bit        Expl.
  0-7   W    Sound length; units of (256-n)/256s  (0-255)
  8-12  -    Not used.
  13-14 R/W  Sound Volume  (0=Mute/Zero, 1=100%, 2=50%, 3=25%)
  15    R/W  Force Volume  (0=Use above, 1=Force 75% regardless of above)
The Length value is used only if Bit 6 in NR34 is set.
4000074h - SOUND3CNT_X (NR33, NR34) - Channel 3 Frequency/Control (R/W)
  Bit        Expl.
  0-10  W    Sample Rate; 2097152/(2048-n) Hz   (0-2047)
  11-13 -    Not used
  14    R/W  Length Flag  (1=Stop output when length in NR31 expires)
  15    W    Initial      (1=Restart Sound)
  16-31 -    Not used
The above sample rate specifies the number of wave RAM digits per second, the
actual tone frequency depends on the wave RAM content, for example:
  Wave RAM, single bank 32 digits   Tone Frequency
  FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0000000000000000  65536/(2048-n) Hz
  FFFFFFFF00000000FFFFFFFF00000000  131072/(2048-n) Hz
  FFFF0000FFFF0000FFFF0000FFFF0000  262144/(2048-n) Hz
  FF00FF00FF00FF00FF00FF00FF00FF00  524288/(2048-n) Hz
  F0F0F0F0F0F0F0F0F0F0F0F0F0F0F0F0  1048576/(2048-n) Hz
4000090h - WAVE_RAM0_L - Channel 3 Wave Pattern RAM (W/R)
4000092h - WAVE_RAM0_H - Channel 3 Wave Pattern RAM (W/R)
4000094h - WAVE_RAM1_L - Channel 3 Wave Pattern RAM (W/R)
4000096h - WAVE_RAM1_H - Channel 3 Wave Pattern RAM (W/R)
4000098h - WAVE_RAM2_L - Channel 3 Wave Pattern RAM (W/R)
400009Ah - WAVE_RAM2_H - Channel 3 Wave Pattern RAM (W/R)
400009Ch - WAVE_RAM3_L - Channel 3 Wave Pattern RAM (W/R)
400009Eh - WAVE_RAM3_H - Channel 3 Wave Pattern RAM (W/R)
This area contains 16 bytes (32 x 4bits) Wave Pattern data which is output by
channel 3. Data is played back ordered as follows: MSBs of 1st byte, followed
by LSBs of 1st byte, followed by MSBs of 2nd byte, and so on - this results in
a confusing ordering when filling Wave RAM in units of 16bit data - ie. samples
would be then located in Bits 4-7, 0-3, 12-15, 8-11.
In the GBA, two Wave Patterns exists (each 32 x 4bits), either one may be
played (as selected in NR30 register), the other bank may be accessed by the
users. After all 32 samples have been played, output of the same bank (or other
bank, as specified in NR30) will be automatically restarted.
Internally, Wave RAM is a giant shift-register, there is no pointer which is
addressing the currently played digit. Instead, the entire 128 bits are
shifted, and the 4 least significant bits are output.
Thus, when reading from Wave RAM, data might have changed its position. And,
when writing to Wave RAM all data should be updated (it'd be no good idea to
assume that old data is still located at the same position where it has been
written to previously).
  GBA Sound Channel 4 - Noise
This channel is used to output white noise. This is done by randomly switching
the amplitude between high and low at a given frequency. Depending on the
frequency the noise will appear 'harder' or 'softer'.
It is also possible to influence the function of the random generator, so the
that the output becomes more regular, resulting in a limited ability to output
Tone instead of Noise.
4000078h - SOUND4CNT_L (NR41, NR42) - Channel 4 Length/Envelope (R/W)
  Bit        Expl.
  0-5   W    Sound length; units of (64-n)/256s  (0-63)
  6-7   -    Not used
  8-10  R/W  Envelope Step-Time; units of n/64s  (1-7, 0=No Envelope)
  11    R/W  Envelope Direction                  (0=Decrease, 1=Increase)
  12-15 R/W  Initial Volume of envelope          (1-15, 0=No Sound)
  16-31 -    Not used
The Length value is used only if Bit 6 in NR44 is set.
400007Ch - SOUND4CNT_H (NR43, NR44) - Channel 4 Frequency/Control (R/W)
The amplitude is randomly switched between high and low at the given frequency.
A higher frequency will make the noise to appear 'softer'.
When Bit 3 is set, the output will become more regular, and some frequencies
will sound more like Tone than Noise.
  Bit        Expl.
  0-2   R/W  Dividing Ratio of Frequencies (r)
  3     R/W  Counter Step/Width (0=15 bits, 1=7 bits)
  4-7   R/W  Shift Clock Frequency (s)
  8-13  -    Not used
  14    R/W  Length Flag  (1=Stop output when length in NR41 expires)
  15    W    Initial      (1=Restart Sound)
  16-31 -    Not used
Frequency = 524288 Hz / r / 2^(s+1)     ;For r=0 assume r=0.5 instead

content.text:
I found no blockers or majors, so this branch can be merged. All findings below are minor.

**What I checked:**
- **Spec match:** The PSG code matches gbatek "GBA Sound Channel 1-4" in every place I checked:
  - **Timer rates:** tone runs at 131072/(2048-n) Hz (16 cycles per duty step), wave at 2097152/(2048-n) Hz (8 cycles per digit), and noise at 524288/r/2^(s+1) with r=0 treated as 0.5.
  - **Noise generator:** XOR 6000h (15-bit) or 60h (7-bit), seeded with 4000h or 40h, output high on carry.
  - **Patterns and banks:** the duty patterns are right. Wave samples play the upper 4 bits first. The CPU reads and writes the bank that is not playing, and two-bank playback starts on the selected bank.
  - **Volumes and counters:** wave volume 0/100/50/25% plus the forced 75%. Length counters are (64-n) and (256-n) at 256 Hz, the sweep runs at 128 Hz (7.8 ms), and the envelope at 64 Hz.
  - **Edge cases:** partial-byte writes to the frequency registers merge correctly. Only writes that include bit 15 restart a channel. Clearing NR30 bit 7 stops channel 3.
  - **Read-back:** write-only bits are masked centrally in `src/io.rs` `readable_bits`, so this branch doesn't need to.
- **Ownership:** clean. The only file changed against main is `src/apu/psg.rs`. The branch also contains a merge of main into itself, which is fine.
- **No per-ROM hacks:** none found.
- **Originality:** clean. "Frame sequencer" is a common Game Boy documentation term, not a gbatek name. Here it is just the 512 Hz rate that the gbatek rates (256/128/64 Hz) divide from, and the author says the phase between them is arbitrary. Nothing points to another emulator's layout.
- **Tests:**
  - `cargo test` passes all 125 tests, including 9 new PSG unit tests covering duty and length, envelope, sweep overflow, wave banks, noise period, restart, partial writes, wave volume and power-off.
  - The wasm release build succeeds with no warnings.
  - `run_rom` on `tonc/snd1-demo.gba` ran for 300 frames without a panic. I did not grade it, as you asked.

**Findings:**

- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/apu/psg.rs:175`: [minor] With sweep shift n=0, `sweep_target` doubles the frequency (or sets it to 0). That follows gbatek's formula literally, but it is the kind of edge case a game might hit. Gbatek is silent on it. Suggested fix: add a comment saying it is deliberate, so a later fix in Phase 5 isn't mistaken for a spec change.
- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/apu/psg.rs:188`: [minor] The doc comment cites "the task brief" as its source, which doesn't help a reader later. Suggested fix: say plainly that gbatek doesn't define what happens above 2047 and that stopping the channel is our choice.
- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/apu/psg.rs:92,338,462,509`: [minor] Register bits are tested with unnamed hex values: `0x0800` (envelope direction), `0x0020` (two-bank mode), `0x0080` (channel 3 playback on), `0x0040` / `>> 6` (bank number) and `0x0008` (sweep direction, 7-bit noise). Suggested fix: name them as constants like `TRIGGER_BIT`, each with a one-line comment.
- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/apu/psg.rs:390`: [minor] `wave_output` does three things in one function: choose the bank and digit, convert the digit to a signed level, and apply the volume. Suggested fix: move the volume part into a small `apply_wave_volume(level, SOUND3CNT_H)` helper.
